newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees good chance to reduce global poverty.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees good chance to reduce global poverty.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Tuesday he saw good prospects for reducing worldwide poverty in the years ahead.

"As we approach the 21st century, we are well positioned to reduce global poverty and encourage sustainable growth," Rubin told the joint Development Committee of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.

"The global economic expansion is relatively stable, with generally low interest rates, steady economic expansion in most developed countries and strong growth in many dynamic developing countries," the Treasury chief added.
In his speech, Rubin urged the World Bank to concentrate its support on helping poor nations that are committed to sound economic policies and poverty reduction.
The aim should be to increase the effectiveness of scarce development assistance, he said. Priority must be given to helping the poor and protecting the environment.
"Excessive military expenditures and subsidies for inefficient state-owned enterprises should be substantially reduced," Rubin added.
The Treasury chief also called for a broad-based attack on corruption, arguing that graft can hurt development.
Rubin suggested that the World Bank transfer some of its profits to the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) to help it through the rest of this century.

He also urged MIGA to boost its gearing ratio so it has more money to provide political risk insurance and other help to developing nations. MIGA, which is an affiliate of the World Bank, is faced with a cash squeeze.
"We believe that the Bank should transfer $300 million of net income to MIGA, in approximately equal instalments over the next two -- or at most -- three years," he said.
